completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed two independent taught-snippet defects in the lean extension: guard invocations missing a lake subcommand (exit 77 no-op) and a hardcoded Theories/ scan root that silently scans nothing in consuming repos. Added lean-src-roots.sh (lakefile.toml-derived, loud-failure resolver), made lean-sorry-census.sh fail loudly on missing/empty targets, routed all taught final-verification and commit-staging snippets through the resolver, verified end-to-end in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic (planted and detected a real sorry), and redeployed into that consuming repo.

memory_candidates.content: When a taught verification snippet must scan 'the project's source', never hardcode a literal directory name (e.g. Theories/) — different consuming repos use different library roots (FormalSystem/, Cslib/, etc.), and a nonexistent literal makes a grep/scan silently examine zero files and report a false-clean result. Instead, derive roots at runtime from the repo's own build manifest (e.g. lakefile.toml [[lean_lib]] entries, applying the build tool's own default rules for missing fields) via ONE shared resolver script that every snippet calls, and make the resolver (and any downstream consumer) exit non-zero naming the root(s) tried whenever nothing resolves or the resolved root holds zero relevant files. 'Scanned and clean' must always be distinguishable from 'scanned nothing.'

When a CLI tool validates its first post-'--' argument against an allowlist of subcommands (e.g. a lake/make/cargo wrapper), a taught invocation example that places a bare argument (like a module/target name) directly after '--' with no subcommand will fail the allowlist check and no-op — and this is easy to copy-paste-propagate because a nearly-identical CORRECT example often sits right next to it. When auditing/fixing such taught snippets, do an EXHAUSTIVE grep across the whole codebase (not spot-checks) extracting every first post-'--' token and checking it against the tool's own allowlist (read from the tool's source, don't hand-copy it) — the same defect tends to recur at 3+ independent sites.
